note: Whether a running machine says hello at once when the person changes its settings at the machine, rather than leaving its receivers to learn it from the next hello. `change` is what was done while the daemon ran: `paired` (a second receiver paired), `folders` (`control folders`), `mode` (`control mode`), `name` (`--rename-machine`), `ask` (`ask off`), `unpaired` (one of two receivers removed), `nothing` (the same settings read again). `expect` is `hello` (one goes out now, and a newly paired receiver is among those it reaches) or `none`. The reference daemon says a hello it sends at once to every receiver it is paired with.

cases.name: a receiver paired while the daemon runs learns at once what the machine takes
a new folder list is said at once
a new mode is said at once
a new name is said at once, so the receiver shows one machine
asking turned off is said at once
a receiver removed tells the others nothing new
the same settings read again say nothing
